key_insight: A high-throughput DFT search identified CuI-based ternary compounds as a rich new family of p-type transparent conductors, including many previously unreported candidates and intrinsically hole-doped semiconductors.
engineering_relevance: These materials could enable more conductive transparent electrodes for transparent electronics and tandem photovoltaics, where robust p-type TCMs are a major bottleneck.
method: Minima hopping method used to explore CuI-based ternary X–Cu–I compounds.
Density functional theory screened candidates for thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and low hole effective mass.
Chemical modulation of the valence band design rules were revisited using the discovered dataset.
evidence_signal: From the computational screen, 58 candidate p-type TCMs were found, 49 of them new, and 20 were degenerate semiconductors with intrinsic hole carriers.
watch_item: The results are computational predictions only, so experimental synthesis and stability under device-relevant conditions still need validation.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
